status_meanings.pending: Not started or not established as implemented
status_meanings.in_progress: One approved bounded task is currently being worked on
status_meanings.blocked: Work cannot continue; document exact blocker

rules: Do not start implementation solely because a task is listed.
Before activating a task, reconcile local repository state with current source, Git and tests.
At most one task may have status in_progress at a time; active_task_id must identify that task or be null.
Do not bypass dependency order or expand an active task into later features.
Use RED -> GREEN -> regression verification for implementation tasks.
Only mark verified after acceptance criteria, actual commands, outcomes and revision are recorded.
Do not silently change roadmap scope or mark planned work implemented.
Do not commit, push, deploy, or alter production resources without authorization.

acceptance_criteria: Multiple implementations can be registered and invoked by name.
Unknown handlers are rejected.

tasks.title: Conditions and Branching
tasks.objective: Evaluate predicates and select configured true/false successor steps.
acceptance_criteria: Both branches are tested.
Condition errors are handled and tested.

evidence.result: Historical implementation evidence (2026-11-11), at 88fe6ed924efd351cb2a10d5cd8f11f326b81006 plus then-uncommitted M3.5 changes, as recorded in the committed PROGRESS.md and docs/HANDOFF.md checkpoint: initialization, tracker validation, pre-activation M3.5 preflight and baseline verifier passed. Preflight is historical and was not rerun for acceptance of the already active task. RED: focused tests exited 1 because SelectConditionSuccessor was undefined at test lines 41, 73, 78 and 93. GREEN: verbose focused tests exited 0 after implementation/gofmt; three test functions and eight subtests passed. Historical post-change verifier exited 1 at race-test setup from sandbox Go-cache denial after tracker, 44 Python tests and Go unit tests passed; Codex reported a permission-enabled rerun exiting 0 with all six checks PASS. The documentation session separately reported Go unit-test setup cache denial followed by a permission-enabled all-six-checks PASS. These historical results were not personally reexecuted by the human approver. Committed test review supports both unchanged acceptance criteria: TRUE selects OnTrue and FALSE selects OnFalse; TRUE/error and FALSE/error return the original error and no successor. Four empty-successor cases establish valid terminal paths with nil error. Each of eight cases runs twice and asserts one predicate invocation per selection attempt, unchanged step/registration counts and duplicate-registration rejection. Unknown handlers (missing, blank, case/padding mismatches and zero-value registry) return no successor/error; ACTION, WAIT, empty and unsupported step types are rejected before predicate invocation. Published implementation: e0e73da376d55cd22c86fdda8d6011af022a9b0a; published documentation checkpoint: 959186046ff3dfd3a86c350027bf7afcd2f509cc. Fresh acceptance reconciliation (2026-11-11) started on clean main at the documentation checkpoint; initialization and tracker validation passed. Live git ls-remote initially exited 128 from sandbox DNS failure; permission-enabled rerun exited 0 confirming published main at 959186046ff3dfd3a86c350027bf7afcd2f509cc. Both focused Go commands initially exited 1 from sandbox build-cache denial; permission-enabled reruns exited 0, including all three test functions and eight subtests. Limitations: callers must validate definitions/successor references and check errors first. Selection returns an ID only; it does not traverse the graph, execute actions, advance a cursor, wait/resume or call repository TryClaim/Complete/Fail. Each attempt reevaluates the predicate; no deduplication, retries, persistence, panic recovery or exactly-once guarantee. Callback side effects and concurrency safety belong to callers; registration must not overlap registry operations across goroutines, populated registries must not be copied, and nil registry pointers are unsupported. No production deployment, cloud integration or end-to-end workflow runner is established. M3.6-M3.10 (sequential actions, wait/resume, lifecycle integration, concurrency/failure verification and milestone acceptance) remain pending and unchanged; M3.6 is not activated. tasks.title: Sequential Action Execution
tasks.objective: Execute configured actions in order and advance progress only after successful steps.
acceptance_criteria: Actions run in required order.
A failed action stops the normal path and returns an error outcome.

tasks.title: Wait and Resume
tasks.objective: Represent delays with resume deadlines and retain an in-memory execution cursor, without sleeping a worker for the entire wait.
acceptance_criteria: Early resume does not advance incorrectly.
Eligible resume continues from the correct step without replaying earlier completed actions in the tested in-memory scenario.
No durable restart guarantee is claimed.

tasks.title: M2 Lifecycle Integration
tasks.objective: Use repository TryClaim for ownership and Complete/Fail for terminal runner outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Success and failure preserve M2 status, version, and history invariants.
Failures use Fail with a nonempty reason; SaveIfVersion is not used to mark FAILED.

tasks.title: Concurrency and Failure Verification
tasks.objective: Test competing execution attempts, invalid ownership, action errors, and duplicate invocations.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate action execution in the tested single-process concurrent scenario.
Failure reasons and lifecycle state remain correct.
No distributed exactly-once guarantee is claimed.

tasks.title: Reusability and Milestone Acceptance
tasks.objective: Run two genuinely different workflows through the same engine and execute full regression verification.
acceptance_criteria: Both workflows run without modifying the engine core.
Existing M1/M2 tests and race checks pass.
Known limitations are documented.
